Carcinoma prostatico ISUP 5 (Gleason 4+5: ISUP 5 (Gleason 4+5) prostate carcinoma of the central-anterior portion, bilateral: PI-RADS 5 in the transition zone
Uomo di 63 anni. PSA 17,3 ng/mL; volume: 63-year-old man. PSA 17.3 ng/mL; prostate volume about 25 mL (PSA density about 0.7 ng/mL²). 3 T prostate MRI (available sequences: axial T2, calculated high-b diffusion and ADC map; dynamic contrast sequences are not in the collection).
PI-RADS 2.1: la sequenza che decide dipe:
PI-RADS 2.1: the deciding sequence depends on the zone. In the peripheral zone, diffusion dominates; in the transition zone, T2 dominates, and diffusion serves to confirm or to raise the score.
In the transition zone, hyperplasia produces well-encapsulated, heterogeneous nodules (“organized”). The tumor, by contrast, is a homogeneous, moderately hypointense area, with ill-defined or lenticular margins, without a capsule, that “erases” the architecture like charcoal smudged with an eraser: T2 = 4 if < 1.5 cm, 5 if ≥ 1.5 cm or with extraprostatic extension.
Here the area occupies the central and anterior part of the gland on both sides, is bright on high b and dark on ADC: PI-RADS 5. Anterior tumors often escape systematic biopsy (which mainly samples the posterior peripheral zone): this is one of the reasons MRI is done before biopsy.
PSA density (PSA divided by volume) helps: above 0.15-0.20 ng/mL² the risk of clinically significant cancer is high; here it is about 0.7.
The report should also describe: relationship to the anterior capsule and the anterior fibromuscular stroma, sphincter and apex, seminal vesicles, lymph nodes and bones in the field of view. A tumor ISUP 4-5 or with PSA above 20 is high risk: staging with PSMA PET (or CT and bone scintigraphy).
Zona di transizione: comanda il T2. Area: Transition zone: T2 dominates. Homogeneous hypointense area with ill-defined margins ≥ 1.5 cm = PI-RADS 5.
Biopsia mirata con fusione RM-ecografia:: MRI-ultrasound fusion targeted biopsy: Gleason 4+5 = 9 (ISUP 5) prostatic adenocarcinoma in all targeted cores, bilateral, up to 17 mm of tumor per core (Prostate-MRI-US-Biopsy collection data).
Qual è la conclusione più adatta?: What is the most appropriate conclusion?
Ampia area ipointensa omogenea in T2, a: Large homogeneous T2 hypointense area with ill-defined margins (“erased charcoal”), in the central and anterior portion of the gland (transition zone), bilateral, at the level of the middle third
La stessa area è iperintensa nelle immag: The same area is hyperintense on high-b images and hypointense on the ADC map (diffusion restriction)
Solo noduli ben capsulati e disomogenei: Only well-encapsulated, heterogeneous nodules in the transition zone (hyperplasia), without homogeneous hypointense areas
Area ipointensa a cuneo in T2 senza rest: Wedge-shaped hypointense area on T2 without diffusion restriction (prostatitis)
